what_its_for: Diazepam is used to treat anxiety, muscle spasms, seizures, and symptoms of alcohol withdrawal. It belongs to a group of medicines called benzodiazepines, which work by calming your brain and nerves.
how_to_take: Take diazepam exactly as your doctor prescribed. You can take it with or without food. If it upsets your stomach, try taking it with a small snack or glass of milk. Swallow tablets whole with a full glass of water. Do not crush, chew, or break the tablets. If you are using the liquid form, measure your dose carefully using the dropper that comes with the medicine — do not use a regular kitchen spoon.
dosing: Your dose depends on your age, weight, medical condition, and how you respond to treatment. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions. Adults are usually started on a low dose and the doctor will slowly adjust it if needed. Never take more than prescribed, and do not take it more often than directed. Do not stop taking diazepam suddenly without talking to your doctor first, as this can cause serious withdrawal symptoms.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still a few hours before your next scheduled dose. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose completely and continue with your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store diazepam at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from light, heat, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to safely dispose of leftover medication.
what_to_avoid: Do not drink alcohol while taking diazepam — this combination can be very dangerous and can cause extreme drowsiness, difficulty breathing, or even death. Avoid taking other medicines that cause drowsiness, such as sleep aids, opioid pain medicines, antihistamines, or other anxiety medicines, unless your doctor has approved them. Do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do anything that requires you to be fully alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice, as it may interact with how your body processes this medicine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: trouble breathing or slow, shallow breathing; extreme drowsiness or difficulty waking up; confusion or unusual behavior; thoughts of harming yourself; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat; yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice); or if your symptoms are getting worse instead of better. Also call your doctor if you feel dependent on the medicine or if you want to stop taking it.
when_it_works: Diazepam usually starts working within 30 to 60 minutes after you take it. For anxiety relief, most people notice an effect fairly quickly. For seizure control or muscle spasms, your doctor will monitor your response over time. The full benefit of the medicine may take a few days to weeks depending on what it is being used for.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and older): Use with extra caution. Older adults are more sensitive to the effects of diazepam and have a higher risk of falls, confusion, and memory problems. Doctors usually start with the lowest possible dose. Pregnancy: Do not take diazepam if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant without talking to your doctor. It may harm the unborn baby. Breastfeeding: Diazepam passes into breast milk and may cause drowsiness or feeding problems in your baby. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: Diazepam may be used in children for certain conditions, but only under close medical supervision. Liver or kidney problems: Your doctor may need to adjust your dose if you have liver or kidney disease.
